Read the walkthrough transcript
  1. Keep copied text, links and images in Clipora’s local workspace.
  2. Open quick access with Ctrl + Alt + V near your destination. Search and choose a saved clip.
  3. Pin useful replies so they stay above ordinary history. Use the item menu for copy, paste and other actions.
  4. Choose black or light appearance, density and image previews.
  5. Keep a portable password-encrypted backup before moving or resetting the app.

The video uses still captures of the actual interface. It does not measure paste speed or demonstrate a live cross-app paste. Try the app with synthetic text to check your own destination.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS.

Before your next copy.

Need a hand? ↗
How is this different from my normal clipboard?+

Clipora keeps a searchable history of supported copies while it runs, with images, pins, collections, transformations and a customizable quick-access window. Press Ctrl+Alt+V to recall a clip. It does not import another application's existing history.

Is Clipora free? What do I need?+

Clipora is free on Microsoft Store. It supports Windows x64, Windows 10 build 19041 or later; Windows 11 is recommended. There are no macOS or mobile clients.

Does my clipboard leave my computer?+

Local history stays on your computer by default. Optional encrypted folder/private-server sync is disabled initially. Update checks contact Microsoft Store or public release metadata; they do not send clipboard content. Trusted macros can access files and networks, so review code before trusting it.

What happens when I close Clipora?+

Closing the workspace leaves Clipora in the Windows tray and recording continues. Pause stops recording; Quit Clipora exits. You can enable Start with Windows in Settings. Export a backup before uninstalling or resetting the Store app.

Can it paste into every application?+

Windows can restrict input into elevated applications; use Copy and manual Ctrl+V there. File clips reference their original files. Very rapid copies may miss intermediate content.
